key_insight: Micropillar compression reveals that in anorthite, mechanical twinning is the easiest deformation mode (~300 MPa CRSS) while slip strength depends strongly on temperature and slip system.
engineering_relevance: These measurements provide direct constitutive inputs for predicting crustal rheology of plagioclase-rich rocks under geological loading conditions.
method: Focused-ion-beam milled ~1 µm micropillars from three crystal orientations of anorthite single crystals.
Compressed 36 pillars inside an SEM at 25, 300, and 800 °C.
Compared activation of twinning and multiple slip systems under a constant displacement rate (~0.001 s⁻¹ strain rate).
evidence_signal: The abstract reports orientation-dependent yielding across 36 tests, with twinning showing a temperature- and strain-rate-insensitive CRSS near 300 MPa and slip becoming easier at higher temperatures.
watch_item: Micropillar tests probe local single-crystal behavior, so scaling these strengths to natural polycrystalline rocks and lower geological strain rates requires caution.
paper_title: Quantification of plastic deformation in anorthite using micropillar compression
